source: We have developed a new event detection algorithm to overcome some limitations of current velocity-based algorithms. It has two major components. First, the new algorithm is endowed with a noise-dependent velocity threshold that is adaptive with respect to different view- ers, different recording situations, and/or varying levels of noise during a whole experiment or a single trial. The automatic adaption of velocity threshold makes our algo- rithm settings-free for users. In most current algorithms, the variable level of noise is disregarded and not auto- matically adjusted for. Instead, the end user must make the important decision of how to deal with noise via the velocity threshold, using his/her subjective judgment or just trusting the default settings of the analysis software.

source: Instead, the algorithm terminates the saccade before the glissade, identifies the glissade as another, short saccade, and inserts an absurdly short fixation in between. source: Given gaze coordinates produced by the eyetracker, an event detector should robustly classify these raw data into events such as fixations, saccades, and smooth pursuit pe- riods, as well as blinks and noise. This may sound fairly straightforward, but the task presents users with several difficulties, among which the selection of threshold is the best known. It has been shown that event detection algo- rithms are very sensitive to the choice of thresholds that they need to distinguish—for example, a saccade sample from a fixation sample (see Blignaut, 2009; Shic, Chawar- ska, & Scassellati, 2008).

source: The aim of this article is to design a velocity-based saccade detection algorithm that addresses many of the limitations of current algorithms. The goal is to develop a data-driven algorithm that leaves as few subjective set- tings to the end user as possible. The improvements in- clude data-driven thresholds for peak and saccade onset/ offset detection, adaptive threshold adjustment based on local noise levels, physical constraints on eye move- ments to exclude noise and jitter, and new recommenda- tions for minimum allowed fixation and saccade dura- tion. Since it is unclear how attention and visual intake are correlated with eye movement in the general case, the proposed algorithm is designed to identify oculomo- tor events in eye movement data and leave the important question of related cognitive processes to the individual researcher.

Now translate the following text: Second, the new algorithm was designed with the ex- plicit goal of detecting glissades. Detecting glissades is appropriate because they exist and have a statistical distribution, like many other eye movement events. If we use algorithms that are not explicit about glissades, their durations will randomly spill over to the fixation or the saccade or will trick the algorithm into output- ting absurdly short fixations, making results less reliable and less comparable. Glissades were found to occur fre- quently (in over half of all the saccades) and had an aver- age duration of about 24 msec. This would add more than 25% to the average saccade duration and about 5% to the average fixation duration. Our algorithm solves all these problems and gives the user control over glissades in the data analysis. In addition, acknowledging and studying glissades as a separate class of eye movements has the potential of opening up new insights on oculomotor con- trol and perception, and data on glissades may be linked to fatigue and neurological disorders (see, e.g., Cuiffreda & Tannen, 1995, p. 39).

In most current algorithms, the variable level of noise is disregarded and not auto- matically adjusted for. Instead, the end user must make the important decision of how to deal with noise via the velocity threshold, using his/her subjective judgment or just trusting the default settings of the analysis software.
translation: 我々は、現在の速度ベースのアルゴリズムに見られるいくつかの制限を克服するため、新しいイベント検出アルゴリズムを開発した。このアルゴリズムには2つの主要な構成要素がある。第一に、新しいアルゴリズムは、観察者間、記録状況間、および実験全体または単一の試行中に変化する雑音レベルに対して適応可能な、雑音依存性の速度閾値を備えている。速度閾値の自動適応により、ユーザーにとってのアルゴリズム設定不要が実現される。ほとんどの現在のアルゴリズムでは、変動する雑音レベルが無視され、自動的に調整されない。代わりに、エンドユーザーは速度閾値を用いて、雑音に対処する方法について、主観的な判断を行うか、分析ソフトウェアのデフォルト設定に頼るという重要な決定を下さなければならない。

source: Since glissade detection is one of the main novelties in the new algorithm, let us start by taking a look at what they are and how they might influence event detection. Figure 1 plots the x-, y-coordinates and angular velocity of a portion of reading data. At the end of the two leftmost saccades, one can clearly see how the eye overshoots its intended target and immediately corrects this by a smaller, saccade-like movement. This movement is known as a dy- namic overshoot (rapid postsaccadic movement; Kapoula, Robinson, & Hain, 1986) or a glissadic overshoot (slower postsaccadic movement; Weber & Daroff, 1972). For sim- plicity, in the remainder of this article, we use the term glissade for all types of movements that happen due to over-undershoots.

source: Eye movement data collected during scene percep- tion originate from the study by Nyström and Holmqvist (2008), where details about the experiment can be found. In short, gaze positions were recorded at 1250 Hz with the SMI HiSpeed eyetracker while 10 subjects watched digitized photographs of “real-world” images on a com- puter screen. source: Several years later, we were in possession of a large data- base of recorded eye movements during reading. M. Nystrӧm kindly made the Matlab (Natick, MA) code available to us. The coding style was remarkably sophisticated, elegant, and efficient. We did find one error in the many lines of code. Although in the present case this error played no role in our analysis, in other contexts it might be very important.{v1}We made minor technical modifications to the code in order to better accommodate our data format and to report out the data as we preferred.One substantive changewe had to make from the start was the sampling rate. The original code was written for data collected from an SMI HiSpeed eyetracker (Teltow, Germany) at 1250 Hz, but our data were collected with an EyeLink 1000 (SR Research, Kanata, ON, Canada) at 1000 Hz. Dr. Nystrӧm informedus that his algorithm was adaptable

source: too many samples are labelled as saccade. But the same result could be interpreted as a PSO that starts too late. We resolved this problem by creating a hierarchy of decisions, described below. In this hierarchy, saccades precede PSOs, so a late transition from a saccade to a PSO would always beclassified as a saccade that ends too late. In this case, the error BPSO Starts Too Late{v1}would never occur.

source: 11.7 deg to the top and 18.5 deg to the bottom. The EyeLink 1000 (SR Research Ltd., Kanata, ON, Canada), a video- oculography system that employs detection of both the pupil and the corneal reflectionto determine gaze position, was used to record eye movements. It records both vertical and horizon- tal eye movements, binocularly. In the present study, only left eye movements were collected. For 298 subjects, we have a mean spatial accuracy of 0.50 (SD{v1}.17, min {v2}.20, max {v3}1.06). For further specifications, see the SR Research website (www.sr-research.com). The sampling rate for our data was 1000 Hz. Prior to each task, a calibration dataset, consisting of nine screen positions (primary position and eight peripheral points), was collected by the EyeLink 1000. A position calibration validation procedure was run immediately after calibration. If there was little error (maximum error {v4}.5 deg, average error {v5}.0 deg), the calibration was accepted. Otherwise, the equipment was readjusted and the calibration was redone. During the recording, before each task, the operator explained the next task (stimulus). The EyeLink 1000 transformed the raw records into gaze position data, in visual angle units, using the calibration data collected at the start of each task. The Stampe (1993) heuristic spike removal algorithm was employed. (It was also used on the data processed for the ONH.) We set the parameter File Filter Setting {v6}on the Eyelink 1000. This means that the File Sample Filter was set to Extra, meaning that the data re- corded would be filtered using a two-stage recursive heu- ristic filter of the type described in the Stampe article. Over the course of several generations of EyeLink eyetrackers, SR Research has made some small, proprie- tary changes to the exact heuristics to further improve their performance, but the fundamental approach remains the same as the one outlined in the Stampe article. Our EyeLink software version was 4.48. Also, blinks were de- tected and removed from the data by the EyeLink 1000. The eye movements were analyzed offline. Only the first 26 s of recordings for each subject were chosen for this study, because one of the subjects chosen randomly fin- ished reading the poem in approximately 26 s, and we wanted the same amount of data from each subject to be represented in each recording.
draft: 上方向11.7度、下方向18.5度。眼球運動を記録するために、瞳孔および角膜反射の両方の検出を用いる動画眼底計測システムであるEyeLink 1000（SR Research Ltd., Kanata, ON, Canada）が使用された。この装置は垂直方向および水平方向の眼球運動を両眼で記録する。本研究では、左眼の眼球運動のみを収集した。298人の被験者について、空間精度の平均値は0.50（SD{v1}.17、最小{v2}.20、最大{v3}1.06）であった。詳細についてはSR Researchのウェブサイト（www.sr-research.com）を参照されたい。本研究のデータのサンプリング周波数は1000 Hzであった。各タスクの前には、9つの画面位置（主視位置および8つの周辺点）からなるキャリブレーションデータセットがEyeLink 1000によって収集された。キャリブレーションの直後には位置キャリブレーション検証手順が実行された。誤差が小さければ（最大誤差{v4}.5度、平均誤差{v5}.0度）、キャリブレーションは承認された。それ以外の場合には装置の再調整が行われ、キャリブレーションが再実施された。記録中に各タスクの前には、オペレーターが次のタスク（刺激）について説明した。EyeLink 1000は、各タスク開始時に収集されたキャリブレーションデータを用いて、生データを視角単位の注視位置データに変換した。Stampe（1993）のヒューリスティックなスパイク除去アルゴリズムが採用された。（ONH処理用データにも同様に使用された。）EyeLink 1000のパラメータ「File Filter Setting {v6}」を設定した。これは、File Sample FilterをExtraに設定することを意味し、生データはStampeの論文で記述されているタイプの2段階再帰的ヒューリスティックフィルタを用いてフィルタリングされることを示している。EyeLink眼動計の複数世代にわたる開発過程において、SR Researchは性能向上を目的として若干の独自的なヒューリスティックの変更を行ったが、根本的なアプローチはStampeの論文で提示されたものと同一である。本研究におけるEyeLinkソフトウェアバージョンは4.48であった。また、瞬目はEyeLink 1000によって検出され、データから削除された。眼球運動はオフラインで分析された。本研究では、各被験者の記録の最初の26秒のみを選択した。これは、ランダムに選ばれた被験者の1人が詩を約26秒で読み終えたためであり、各記録において同一量のデータが代表されるようにしたかったからである。

source: We must acknowledge that this article was written in the belief that the classification of eye movements by human be- ings can be a gold standard. We are aware that Hooge, Niehorster, Nystrom, Andersson, and Hessels (2017) have stated that this view cannot be supported. We disagree with Hooge et al. (2017) and believe their analysis is based on an incomplete interrater reliability study. They studied the reli- ability of experienced oculomotor researchers at a single point in time, without any rater training or consensus discussions. There is a very large literature on the beneficial effects of rater training (Abaza & Ross, 2009; Abbo,Okello, & Nakku, 2013; Alcott, Swann, & Grafham, 1999; Angkaw, Tran, & Haaga, 2006; Bank et al., 2002; Buijze, Guitton, van Dijk, Ring, & the Science of Variation Group, 2012; Chan & Yiu, 2002; Chapman et al., 2016; Cusick, Vasquez, Knowles, & Wallen, 2005; Degenhardt, Snider, Snider, & Johnson, 2005; Haj-Ali & Feil, 2006; Istriana et al., 2013; Iwarsson & Reinholt Petersen, 2012; Lievens, 2001; Lou et al., 2014; Lundh, Kowalski, Sundberg, & Landen, 2012; Magnan & Maklebust, 2009; Mist, Ritenbaugh, & Aickin, 2009; Rosen et al., 2008; Sattler, McKnight, Naney, & Mathis, 2015;

source: Extend artifact blocks backward and forward in time It is reasonable to assume that some signal before and after an artifact might also be contaminated by the artifact, so both algorithms extend the data marked as artifact forward and backward in time. The two algorithms use the identical meth- od, but the thresholds used are completely different. For the ONH, a velocity threshold is set to be the median of the entire velocity signal (all samples in the recording) multiplied by 2.0. This is in contrast to the threshold described by Nystrӧm and Holmqvist (2010), page 193, which states that the threshold is the median of the entire signal but not multi- plied by 2. Artifacts are extended both forward and backward in time until the velocity is less than or equal to this threshold. For the 20 subjects in the present study, the median velocity threshold value was 5.59 (25th percentile {v1}.03, 75th percen- tile {v2}.43). We found that, for our data, this threshold led to the removal of much more signal before and after each artifact block than was reasonable when compared to the ground truth represented by visual inspection. For the MNH, we computed our own threshold. First, we divided the signal into two cate- gories: samples in which the velocity was above 100°/s and samples in which the velocity was below 100°/s. We consid- ered the velocity samples below 100°/s to be a crude estimate of the velocity during fixation. Any Bfixation{v3}blocks of con- tinuous samples that were shorter than the minimum fixation duration (for MNH: 0.030 s) were excluded from further anal- ysis. To obtain the most stable fixation velocity values, for each remaining fixation block, data were rejected that were within 5 ms of the start and end of each fixation block. This procedure would leave in place only the central portions of each fixation block, where the signal would likely be most stable. We combined the velocities from these remaining fix- ation samples and computedthe 90th percentile of the velocity noise distribution. This is the only adaptive threshold in the MNH. We used this as our threshold for deciding how much data to exclude before and after each artifact block. (The MNH also uses this threshold to determine the end of a PSO{v4}see below{v5}.) source: Schredl, Burchert, & Gabatin, 2004; Solah et al., 2015; Staelens et al., 2014; Store-Valen et al., 2015; Taninishi et al., 2016). There is also a literature on the beneficial effects of having consensus discussions and employing consensus guidelines (Beerbaum et al., 2009; Degenhardt et al., 2005; Foppen, van der Schaaf, Beek, Verkooijen, & Fischer, 2016; Iwarsson & Reinholt Petersen, 2012; Meade et al., 2000; Weinstock et al., 2001). The first author of this article has conducted many human interrater reliability studies, with humans classifying complex signals, images, or behaviors, over his career. In no case, upon first testing, were humans found to be reliable. However, using an iterative process of assessing reliability, having consensus discussions,and devel- oping consensus guidelines has always led to much higher, and quite useful levels of interrater reliability. In his view, human raters are generally not reliable in rating complex phe- nomena without training and consensus discussion.

source: One caveat of the present study is that, given that the two algorithms smooth the data to different extents, it was possible for raters to determine which of the two algorithms classified the data being scored. We could not think of a way around this, but it is a threat to the extent to which the recordings were Bblindly{v1}rated. Furthermore, we make no claim that our algorithm is bet- ter, in every instance, with every kind of eye movement data. We had only our sample of subjects studied with theEyeLink 1000 at 1000 Hz to evaluate during a reading task, and, for the time being, our results must be considered limited in this way.

source: Description of the general approach to finding saccades in the MNH The general approach to finding saccades in the MNH is illustrated in Fig. 2B. The saccade peak velocity threshold was fixed at 55°/s, and the saccade subthreshold was fixed at 45°/s. (We question the need for the saccade subthreshold, but have not studied its role sufficiently to decide whether it could be dropped without affecting classification performance.) There must be two samples above the saccade peak velocity threshold for a set of samples tobelabeled as the peakportion of a saccade. To find the start of a saccade, the algorithm steps backward, one sample at a time, to see if the velocity crosses below the saccade subthresh- old. If the samples do cross this threshold, then the algorithm steps backward, one sample at a time, until a local velocity min- imum is found. source: The MNH algorithm, with fixed thresholds for classifying saccades, performed much better than the adaptive method employed by the ONH algorithm. Although Nystrӧm and Holmqvist (2010) emphasize the value of adaptive thresholds, it seems to the present authors that Nystrӧm and Holmqvist do not provide either a theoretical or empirical foundation for the use of adaptive filters. It is not obvious that thresholds for saccade definition, or any event definition, should be adjusted for the level of fixation noise in a recording. The approach seems reasonable, and apparently works well with Nystrӧm and Holmqvist’s data. But the opposite notion, that the veloc- ity thresholds for classifying eye movement events should be constant across subjects, is also reasonable. With adaptive thresholds, the definition of a saccade, for example, is formal- ly different for each subject, and even for the same saccade occurring in different contexts in the same recording. Why should this be so? Using the same thresholds for each subject lead to events that are identically defined across subjects. In our context, in which we use eye movements to biometrically recognize humans at various time intervals, the same event definition will lead to more stable classification results and better biometric performance.As applied to our data,the adap- tive thresholds for saccade peak velocity detection are often unreasonably small (10°–20°/s), whereas, Nystrӧm and Holmqvist report a mean value of 33°/s. Since these adaptive thresholds are based on velocity noise during fixation, it would appear that our data were substantially less noisy than theirs. This is true despite our use of much less smoothing. If we were to try to reinstate the adaptive filter approach going forward, we would use statistical metrics that match the highly skewed distribution of velocity noise during fixation, and set a lower limit on the threshold levels.
draft: 固定しきい値を用いたMNHアルゴリズムは、ONHアルゴリズムが採用する適応的手法よりもはるかに優れた性能を発揮した。NystrӧmとHolmqvist（2010）は適応的しきい値の価値を強調しているが、現在の著者らには、NystrӧmとHolmqvistが適応フィルタの使用に対して理論的または実証的な根拠を提供していないように思われる。固定時の雑音レベルに応じて、サッケード定義や他のイベント定義のしきい値を調整すべきであるとは明らかではない。このアプローチは妥当に思われ、NystrӧmとHolmqvistのデータでは実際によく機能しているように見える。しかし、眼球運動イベントを分類するための速度しきい値が被験者間で一定であるべきという逆の考え方も妥当である。適応的しきい値を用いる場合、たとえばサッケードの定義は各被験者で正式に異なり、同じ記録内でも異なる文脈における同一サッケードに対しても異なることになる。なぜこのようなことが必要なのだろうか？すべての被験者に対して同じしきい値を使用すれば、イベントの定義が被験者間で同一となる。本研究の文脈では、複数の時間間隔における人間の生体認証に眼球運動を用いるため、同じイベント定義によりより安定した分類結果と優れた生体認証性能が得られる。我々のデータに適用すると、適応的しきい値によるサッケードピーク速度検出はしばしば不自然に小さい（10°–20°/s）となる一方で、NystrӧmとHolmqvistは平均値として33°/sを報告している。これらの適応的しきい値は固定時の速度雑音に基づいているため、我々のデータは彼らのデータよりも著しくノイズが少ないように思われる。これは、我々がはるかに少ない平滑化を用いているにもかかわらず真実である。今後適応フィルタアプローチを再導入しようとする場合、固定時の速度雑音の極めて歪んだ分布に適合する統計的指標を使用し、しきい値レベルに下限を設けることになるだろう。

source: In Fig. 8, we show a saccade that, when scored by the ONH, ends so late that the saccade includes a portion of the subsequent PSO. Here we see a saccade that is classified as ending too late for the ONH algorithm but does not end too late when classified by the MNHalgorithm. Note that in this case the ONH-classified saccade includes part of the adjacent PSO, but the MNH- classified saccade ends before the PSO. This occurs because the PSO immediately following the saccade begins at a velocity above the saccade subthreshold (in this case, 8.7°/s). We think that this is an unreasonably small saccade subthreshold that is produced by the adaptive methods for the ONH. The MNH algorithm, which uses more reasonable and fixed thresholds for saccade detection, has no problem recognizing the PSO as a PSO.
draft: 図8に示すように、ONHによってスコア付けされたサッケードは、終了が非常に遅いため、その後のPSO（サッケード後振動）の一部を含んでしまう。ここでは、ONHアルゴリズムによる分類では終了が遅すぎるとして分類されるサッケードが、MNHアルゴリズムによる分類では過剰に遅れていないことがわかる。この場合、ONHによって分類されたサッケードは隣接するPSOの一部を含んでいるが、MNHによって分類されたサッケードはPSOの開始前に終了している。これは、サッケードの直後に続くPSOが、サッケードの下限閾値（この場合8.7°/s）を超える速度で開始するためである。我々は、このように非常に小さなサッケード下限閾値は、ONHに適応的手法によって生じた不自然な結果であると考える。MNHアルゴリズムは、より妥当で固定されたサッケード検出閾値を使用しているため、PSOをPSOとして認識する問題がない。

source: that many, if not most, saccades will appear to start too early in the position trace. Therefore, after we have found the local min- imum, we step forward a variable number of samples (depending on the number of samples between the point at which a saccade passes below the saccade subthreshold and the point of local minimum) to mark the start of each saccade. In the case of Fig. 2B, we stepped forward five samples. To find the end of a sac- cade, the velocity must cross under the saccade subthreshold,and then, moving forward one sample at a time, the local velocity minimum is once again found. If the saccade is followed by a PSO, then this local velocity minimum is the saccade end point. If the saccade is not followed by a PSO, then we step backward a variable number of samples (also depending on the number of samples between the point at which a saccade passes below the saccade subthreshold and the point of local minimum) to mark the end of the saccade. In the case of Fig. 2B, we stepped back five samples.

source: Figure 12E presents the data for the error Bfixation not detected.{v1}These represent 6.29% of all errors. An average of approximately ten fixations were not detected per recording for the ONH. This error almost never occurred for the data scored with the MNH, but many more fixations went unde- tected when scored by the ONH than when scored by the MNH. A substantial number of these occurred near anartifact. The ONH leaves unclassified what we would consider per- fectly good fixation periods before and after artifacts.

source: In Fig. 9, we show an example of the different per- formance of the two algorithms near a blink artifact. The EyeLink 1000 automatically detects blinks and re- places the data during the blink with NaN values. For display purposes, during blinks, we set the horizontal and vertical position to 0.0, and set the velocity to 300. These blink artifacts are shown in white. Both algorithms also typically exclude some data before and after such blinks. These periods are also shown in white. Note how, for the ONH, the fixation periods before and after an artifact period are not scored. These fixation periods are properly scored with the MNH. The ONH defines the set of all potential fixa- tions as those periods that are not saccades and not PSOs. Therefore, the stretch of the recording that starts near 1,350 msand ends near 1,875 ms is not considered as a potential fixation period because it contains an artifact. The MNH defines the set of all potential fixa- tions as those periods that are not saccades and not PSOs and not artifacts. Therefore, the periods from 1,350 to 1,520 and from 1,730 to 1,875 are considered as potential fixations. We think that these are fixation periods and should be counted as such.
draft: 図9に、二つのアルゴリズムが瞬目アーティファクト付近で示す異なる性能の例を示す。EyeLink 1000は瞬目を自動検出し、瞬目中にデータをNaN値に置き換える。表示目的のために、瞬目中は水平位置および垂直位置を0.0に設定し、速度を300に設定する。これらの瞬目アーティファクトは白色で示されている。両方のアルゴリズムは通常、このような瞬目前後にあるデータの一部を除外する。これらの期間も白色で示されている。ONHでは、アーティファクト期間の前後の固視期間がスコア付けされていないことに注目されたい。一方、MNHではこれらの固視期間が適切にスコア付けされている。ONHは、すべての潜在的固視を、サッケードでもなくPSO（サッケード後振動）でもない期間として定義する。したがって、1,350 ms付近から始まり1,875 ms付近で終わる記録の区間はアーティファクトを含んでいるため、潜在的固視期間とは見なされない。一方、MNHは、すべての潜在的固視を、サッケードでもなくPSO（サッケード後振動）でもなくアーティファクトでもない期間として定義する。したがって、1,350から1,520および1,730から1,875の期間は潜在的固視と見なされる。これらが固視期間であると考えており、それらを固視とカウントすべきであると考える。

source: typically during blinks, when the EyeLink 1000 does not return a position value, but rather indicates missing data (Bnot a number,{v1}or NaN). The IRF interpolates across such blinks, treats the interpolated data as if they were good data, and attempts to classify such periods like all the good data in the recording. During postprocessing, the IRF removes the longer blink periods from classifica- tion. For our evaluationof theIRF, we simply declared all of these blink periods as noise/artifacts. Both the ONH and the MNH exclude some data before and after each blink (Bperi-blink{v2}data). Although the IRF claims to do this during postprocessing, our results indicate that no such postprocessing step was actually conducted (see be- low). The IRF results are severely contaminated because the IRF attempts to classify these peri-blink recording periods. We have many cases in which the IRF classifies what is obviously noise as fixation, saccade, or PSO. If these types of artifactual events are not handled properly, we see events in the midst of noise/artifact, where noise is classified as a saccade of 1-ms duration. These 1-ms Bsaccades{v3}can have extremely high velocities (700°/s and above). Again, this is not supposed to happen with the IRF. source: Nystrӧm and Holmqvist have published a method for the classification of eye movements during reading (ONH) (Nyström & Holmqvist, 2010). When we applied this algorithm to our data, the results were not satisfactory, so we modified the algorithm (now the MNH) to better classify our data. The changes included: (1) reducing the amount of signal filtering, (2) excluding a new type of noise, (3) removing several adaptive thresholds and replacing them with fixed thresholds, (4) changing the way that the start and end of each saccade was determined, (5) employing a new algorithm for detecting PSOs, and (6) allowing a fixation period to either begin or end with noise. A new method for the evaluation of classification algorithms is presented. It was designed to provide comprehensive feedback to an algorithm developer, in a time-efficient manner, about the types and numbers of classification errors that an algorithm produces. This evaluation was conducted by three expert raters independently, across 20 randomly chosen recordings, each classified by both algorithms. The MNH made many fewer errors in determiningwhen saccades start and end, and it also detected some fixations and saccades that the ONH did not. The MNH fails to detect very small saccades. We also evaluated two additional algorithms: the EyeLink Parser and a more current, machine-learning-based algorithm. The EyeLink Parser tended to find more saccades that ended too early than did the other methods, and we found numerous problems with the output of the machine-learning-based algorithm.
draft: NystrӧmおよびHolmqvistは、読書中の眼球運動の分類に関する手法を発表した（ONH）（Nyström & Holmqvist, 2010）。このアルゴリズムを我々のデータに適用したところ、結果が満足できなかったため、我々はこのアルゴリズムを改良した（現在のMN H）。改良内容は以下の通りである：（1）信号フィルタリングの量を減少させること、（2）新たな種類の雑音を除外すること、（3）いくつかの適応的しきい値を削除し、固定しきい値に置き換えること、（4）各サッケードの開始および終了の決定方法を変更すること、（5）PSO（サッケード後振動）検出のための新しいアルゴリズムを採用すること、（6）固視期間が雑音で始まるか終了するかを許容すること。眼球運動分類アルゴリズムの評価のための新たな手法が提示された。この評価は、アルゴリズム開発者に対して、時間効率よく、アルゴリズムが生成する分類誤りの種類および数について包括的なフィードバックを提供することを目的として設計された。この評価は、20件のランダムに選ばれた記録について、3名の専門評価者が独立して行った。各記録は両方のアルゴリズムによって分類された。MN Hはサッケードの開始および終了を決定する際に、ONHよりもはるかに少ない誤りを犯した。また、MN HはONHが検出できなかったいくつかの固視およびサッケードも検出した。しかし、MN Hは非常に小さなサッケードを検出できない。さらに、2つの追加アルゴリズムについても評価を行った：EyeLink Parserおよびより最近の機械学習ベースのアルゴリズム。EyeLink Parserは他の手法よりも終了が早すぎるサッケードを多く検出した。また、機械学習ベースのアルゴリズムの出力には多数の問題が見られた。

For the MNH, potential fixations that do not have more samples than the minimum fixationduration (30 samples of 1 ms each, with the MNH at 1000 Hz) are unclassified. We chose 30 ms as the minimum fixation duration, as opposed to the 40-ms minimum employed by the ONH. We made this choice after inspecting fixations in the range of 30–40 ms in duration. All the fixations we observed in this range appeared to be valid fixations. The maximum difference between any two points in the potential fixation block must be smaller than 2 deg, for both the horizontal and vertical position signals. All potential fixation blocks that pass these criteria are considered true fixations.
draft: 除外は正当化されない。なぜなら、MNHは完全に良好な固視期間と見なせる多くの期間を固視としてスコアする一方で、ONHはそのような期間をスコアしないからである。以下では、この理由によりONHが検出できなかった固視の例を見る。MNHにおいて、最小固視持続時間（MNHが1000 Hzの場合、1 msごとに30サンプル）よりもサンプル数が少ない潜在的固視は未分類となる。我々は、ONHが用いている40ミリ秒の最小固視持続時間ではなく、30ミリ秒を最小固視持続時間として選択した。この選択は、30～40ミリ秒の範囲にある固視を検討した結果である。この範囲内で観察したすべての固視は有効な固視と見なされた。潜在的固視ブロック内の任意の2点間の最大差は、水平および垂直位置信号の両方において2度未満でなければならない。これらの基準を満たすすべての潜在的固視ブロックは真の固視とみなされる。

source: First, the EyeLink Parser does not classify PSOs, and there were many PSOs in these recordings. We understand that PSOs are intended to be ignored by the EyeLink Parser. We also under- stand that, for certain real-time applications, the failure to detect PSOs may still allow for some meaningful online calculations. Nonetheless, PSOsarereal events (although they may not be real eye movements; Hooge, Holmqvist, & Nystrom, 2016; Nystrom, Hooge, & Holmqvist, 2013), and we consider the fail- ure of this algorithm to detect them is a flaw in the parser, espe- cially when it is used for offline analysis. The ONH found 1,051 PSOs, and the MNH found 1,350 PSOs. Since our focus is on offline analysis, from our point of view the failure to detect these PSOs is considered to generate classification errors. Second, all blink periods (missing data) are both preceded and followed by Bsaccades.{v1}SR Research refers to these events as Bblink- saccades,{v2}and makes no judgment regarding whether the sac- cades are true saccades or artifacts. In our sample, all such events were artifacts. SR Research informs users in its user manual that these events should be removed, so we will henceforth consider them removed. During online processing, there is not sufficient time to discriminate between the blink–saccades and regular sac- cades, and therefore these events remain classified as saccades. It is up to the user to remove them.
draft: まず、EyeLink ParserはPSO（サッケード後振動）を分類しない。これらの記録には多くのPSO（サッケード後振動）が存在した。我々は、PSO（サッケード後振動）がEyeLink Parserによって無視されることを意図していることを理解している。また、特定のリアルタイム応用において、PSO（サッケード後振動）の検出に失敗しても、依然としていくつかの意味のあるオンライン計算が可能であることも理解している。しかし、PSO（サッケード後振動）は実際のイベントである（ただし、それらが実際の眼球運動であるとは限らない；Hooge, Holmqvist, & Nystrom, 2016; Nystrom, Hooge, & Holmqvist, 2013）。したがって、このアルゴリズムがPSO（サッケード後振動）を検出できないことは、特にオフライン分析に使用される場合、パーサーの欠陥であると考える。ONHは1,051個のPSO（サッケード後振動）を検出し、MNHは1,350個のPSO（サッケード後振動）を検出した。我々の焦点はオフライン分析にあるため、これらのPSO（サッケード後振動）を検出できないことは分類エラーを引き起こすとみなす。第二に、すべての瞬目期間（欠損データ）は、Bサッケードによって前後されている。{v1}SR ResearchはこれらのイベントをB瞬目-サッケードと呼ぶ{v2}、サッケードが真のサッケードであるかアーティファクトであるかについていかなる判断も行わない。我々のサンプルでは、これらすべてのイベントはアーティファクトであった。SR Researchはそのユーザーマニュアルで、これらのイベントは削除すべきであるとユーザーに通知しているため、以降それらを削除されたものとして扱う。オンライン処理においては、瞬目-サッケードと通常のサッケードを区別する十分な時間が存在しないため、これらのイベントは依然としてサッケードとして分類されたままとなる。それらの削除はユーザーの責任である。

source: The Bsaccade starts too early{v1}error type accounted for 52% of all errors. The median number of saccades that start too early is always above 75 for ONH and less than 26 or so for the MNH. Given the very high numbers of saccades that start too early when scored by the ONH, we wondered what percentage of all saccades were scored with this error. These results are presented in Fig. 12B. A median of 78% of all saccades started too early for the ONH, whereas for the MNH this result was 19%. For all raters, more than 70% of all saccades started too early for the ONH, and fewer than 30% forthe MNH.

source: Figure 12C presents the data for the error Bsaccade endstoo late.{v1}There were many more of these errors when scored by the ONH than when scored by the MNH. These errors were 30.26% of all errors. The differences between the ONH and MNH are great and highly statistically significant, and the effect sizes (d) are huge. source: The EyelinkParser does not classify PSOs. Although this may or may not be an issue for those who use the algorithm for online processing and decision making, in our view, it is def- initely an issue for offline analysis. There were approximate 1,000 PSOs in the recordings analyzed herein for 520 total seconds analyzed, so approximately two PSOs per second were missed. The EyeLink Parser does an excellent job deter- mining the timing of saccade onset, but it tends to classify more saccades that end too early than either the ONH or the MNH.

source: Given the absence of methods to handle unusual or artifac- tual events in the IRF, many more noise periods were classi- fied as fixations by this method than by the ONH and MNH methods. The IRF also had more noise periods classified as saccades than the MNH, but not than the ONH. Many more fixation periods were misclassified as PSOs for the IRF than for the ONH or, moredramatically, for the MNH. The IRF had fewer fixations and PSOs that were not detected than the ONH. The IRF had no saccades that started too early, whereas the MNH and, especially, the ONH had many more such events. Although the numbers are small, the IRF had more saccades that ended too early than either the ONH or the MNH. The IRF has fewer Bsaccades that end too late{v1}errors than either of the other algorithms, although the effect was statistically significant only versus the ONH. The IRF has significantly more PSOs that end too early than either other algorithm. The IRF also has more PSOs that end too late than both algorithms, but this increase was statistically significant versus the MNH only.

source: Detecting PSOs with the ONH algorithm The ONH algorithm for detecting PSOs is illustrated in Fig. 4A and B. The ONH defines two types of PSOs, Bweak{v1}(Fig. 4A) and Bstrong{v2}(Fig. 4B). The ONH searches for evidence of a velocity peak from the end of the saccade to 40 ms (minimum fixation dura- tion) after the end of the saccade. This does not mean that the entire PSO must be completed in this window, just that a poten- tial PSOis not a PSO if it does not meet the peak velocity criteria in this window. Weak PSOs occur when the velocity during this period crosses above the local saccade velocity threshold. Strong PSOs occur when the velocity during this period crosses above the saccade peak velocity threshold. If the velocity during this period does not cross above the local saccade velocity threshold, then no PSO is present. Each time the signal crosses above and below this threshold, one potential weak PSO is defined. The velocity during this period can cross above and below the local saccade velocity threshold more than once, as in Fig. 4A. In this case, the event is labeled as a weak PSO, with two weak PSO peaks. The end of the PSO is the first local velocity minimum after the velocity crosses below the local saccade velocity threshold for the last time within this 40-ms win- dow. This local velocity minimum must occur within 80 ms of the end of the previous saccade.
draft: ONHアルゴリズムによるPSO（サッケード後振動）の検出 ONHアルゴリズムによるPSO（サッケード後振動）の検出は図4Aおよび図4Bに示されている。ONHはPSO（サッケード後振動）を2種類定義する。弱いPSO{v1}（図4A）と強いPSO{v2}（図4B）。ONHは、サッケードの終了からサッケード終了後40 ms（最小固視持続時間）までの間に速度ピークの証拠を検索する。これは、PSO（サッケード後振動）全体がこのウィンドウ内で完了しなければならないという意味ではない。むしろ、このウィンドウ内において速度ピーク基準を満たさない場合は、潜在的なPSO（サッケード後振動）はPSO（サッケード後振動）とは見なされない。弱いPSO（サッケード後振動）は、この期間中の速度が局所的サッケード速度閾値を上回るときに発生する。強いPSO（サッケード後振動）は、この期間中の速度がサッケードピーク速度閾値を上回るときに発生する。この期間中の速度が局所的サッケード速度閾値を上回らない場合、PSO（サッケード後振動）は存在しない。信号がこの閾値を上回りかつ下回るたびに、1つの潜在的な弱いPSO（サッケード後振動）が定義される。この期間中の速度は、図4Aのように局所的サッケード速度閾値を複数回上回り下回ることがある。この場合、イベントは弱いPSO（サッケード後振動）としてラベル付けされ、2つの弱いPSO（サッケード後振動）ピークを持つ。PSO（サッケード後振動）の終了は、この40 msウィンドウ内において最後に局所的サッケード速度閾値を下回った後に、最初の局所的速度最小値である。この局所的速度最小値は、前のサッケードの終了から80 ms以内に発生しなければならない。

source: In conclusion, we have modified the original Nystrӧm and Holmqvist (2010) algorithm (ONH) so that we now have a new algorithm, the modified Nystrӧm and Holmqvist method (MNH). It makes dramatically fewer errors, with our data, in saccade timing, and it detects fixations and saccades that remain unclassified by the ONH. The MNH never has complete failures, whereas in some cases the ONH did completely fail. The MNH algorithm does not detect very small saccades, however. The IRF algorithm of Zemblys et al. (2018) does a very poor job of dealing with unusual or artifactual noise in recordings and produces PSO classifica- tions that do not look like PSOs. At this stage, we cannot recommend its use. The EyeLink Parser misses all PSOs and tends tofind saccadesthat end too early, but it does very well detecting the timing of the onset of saccades.

source: Before one can evaluate an algorithm, one first needs to establish the goals of the algorithm. For example, one goal might be to classify the raw data, another might be to classify the smoothed data, and a third might be to classify the velocity trace. Because the ONH employs a Savitzky–Golay filter with a window length for our data of 19ms, and given the fact that this filter would delay the resulting smoothed position and velocity calculation by 9 ms and that this filterdelay was never corrected in the original code, the algorithm could not be intended to classify the raw position signal. (Although Nyström & Holmqvist, 2010, claim that the delay is removed, this is not correct.{v1}We provide more information about this issue below.) Although there is no explicit mention of this, it seems much more likely that the algorithm was designed to classify the smoothed position trace rather than the velocity trace, since classification of the position trace is typically what is desired.

source: We employed a custom graphical user interface programto view the vertical and horizontal position traces as well as a radial velocity trace. The program displayed 1 s of data per page. Fixations were shown in red, saccades in green, PSOs in blue, artifacts in white, and unclassified data in black. The program was designed with a built-in magnifying function—if you clicked the left mouse button at any point in the signal trace, the region where you clicked was magnified by a factor of 10 so that individual samples could be discerned. Pushbuttons brought up dialogs to count the number of any error type per page. All the error classification results were written to an output file for further analysis.
draft: 我々は、垂直方向および水平方向の位置トレースならびに径方向速度トレースを表示するためのカスタムグラフィカルユーザーインターフェースプログラムを使用した。このプログラムは1ページあたり1秒分のデータを表示した。固視は赤色で示され、サッケードは緑色で示され、PSO（サッケード後振動）は青色で示され、アーティファクトは白色で示され、未分類データは黒色で示された。このプログラムは内蔵された拡大機能を備えており、信号トレース上の任意の点で左マウスボタンをクリックすると、クリックした領域が10倍に拡大されて個々のサンプルを識別できるようにした。プッシュボタンにより、各ページあたりの任意のエラー種別の数をカウントするためのダイアログが表示された。すべてのエラー分類結果は、さらなる分析のために出力ファイルに記録された。

source: We wanted to compare the performance of the two algo- rithms, but we were interested particularly in the issues that other algorithm developers would want to have addressed. As one example, for saccade initiation, we wanted to count the number of times each algorithm detected the onset of a sac- cade too early, on the basis of human expert judgment. Another example would be to measure the number offixation periods each algorithm failed to detect. This type of informa- tion would directly assist the algorithm developer in focusing exactly on specific problematic decisions the programs need to make.
draft: 我々は2つのアルゴリズムの性能を比較したかったが、他のアルゴリズム開発者が解決してほしいと考える問題に特に注目していた。たとえば、サッケード開始に関して、人間の専門家判断に基づいて各アルゴリズムがサッケードの開始を過剰に早期に検出した回数をカウントしたかった。もう一つの例は、各アルゴリズムが検出できなかった固視期間の数を測定することである。このような情報は、アルゴリズム開発者がプログラムが判断しなければならない特定の問題点に正確に注目するのを直接支援するだろう。

source: The mean is a poor choice to represent the central tendency of such a distribution. The median is a better choice. The standard deviation is likewise a poor choice to represent the spread of such a distribution. Some sort of percentile measures (e.g., the inter- quartile range or something similar) would be a better choice.We believe that the failure of the ONH algorithm to properly char- acterize the central tendency and spread of these distributions is responsible for a number of classification errors produced by the ONH.
draft: 平均はこのような分布の中心傾向を表すために不適切な選択である。中央値の方がより良い選択である。標準偏差もまた、このような分布のばらつきを表すために不適切な選択である。四分位範囲やそれと類似したある種の百分位数指標（percentile measures）の方がより良い選択である。我々は、ONHアルゴリズムがこれらの分布の中心傾向およびばらつきを適切に特徴付けられなかったことが、ONHによって生じる多数の分類誤差の原因であると考えている。
translation: 平均はこのような分布の中心傾向を表すために不適切な選択である。中央値の方がより良い選択である。標準偏差もまた、このような分布のばらつきを表すために不適切な選択である。四分位範囲やそれと類似したある種の百分位数指標（e.g., the inter-quartile range or something similar）の方がより良い選択である。我々は、ONHアルゴリズムがこれらの分布の中心傾向およびばらつきを適切に特徴付けられなかったことが、ONHによって生じる多数の分類誤差の原因であると考えている。

source: In the original article, Nystrӧm and Holmqvist (2010) raised a concern that the Stampe (1993) heuristic spike filter employed by the EyeLink system might have the effect of removing the number of PSOs. Since bothdata-recording sys- tems applied the Stampe filter, and both found many PSOs, this concern was apparently unfounded. The algorithms did not differ in terms of the time spent making PSOs.
draft: 元の論文において、Nystrӧm と Holmqvist（2010）は、EyeLink システムが採用する Stampe（1993）のヒューリスティックなスパイクフィルタが PSO の数を削除する効果を持つ可能性があると懸念した。両方のデータ記録システムが Stampe フィルタを適用しており、両方とも多数の PSO を検出したため、この懸念は明らかに根拠がなかった。アルゴリズム間では、PSO を行うために要した時間に差は認められなかった。
translation: 元の論文において、Nyström と Holmqvist（2010）は、EyeLink システムが採用する Stampe（1993）のヒューリスティックなスパイクフィルタが、PSO の数を削除する効果を持つ可能性があると懸念した。両方のデータ記録システムが Stampe フィルタを適用しており、両方とも多数の PSO を検出したため、この懸念は明らかに根拠がなかった。アルゴリズム間では、PSO を行うために要した時間に差は認められなかった。

source: During the review process, it was agreed that we would also compare both the ONH and the MNH to two additional algorithms, the EyeLink Parser (SR Research Ltd, Ottawa, Ontario, Canada) and a modern, machine-learning-based eye movement classification algorithm (Zemblys, Niehorster, Komogortsev, & Holmqvist, 2018). The EyeLink Parser is provided with an EyeLink eye movement device similar to the one employed by the EyeLink 1000 herein. This compar- ison allowed us todocumentthe performance of the MNH as compared to a very commonly employed alternative algo- rithm. It is important to note that the EyeLink Parser is a real-time, online algorithm and was not designed to classify PSOs.
draft: レビュー過程において、ONHおよびMNHの両方を、EyeLink Parser（SR Research Ltd, オタワ, オンタリオ州, カナダ）および現代的な機械学習ベースの眼球運動分類アルゴリズム（Zemblys, Niehorster, Komogortsev, & Holmqvist, 2018）という2つの追加アルゴリズムと比較することに合意した。EyeLink Parserは、本稿で使用されているEyeLink 1000と同様のEyeLink眼球運動装置とともに提供される。この比較により、MNHの性能を非常に一般的に用いられる代替アルゴリズムと比較して記録することができた。重要な点として、EyeLink Parserはリアルタイム、オンラインアルゴリズムであり、PSO（サッケード後振動）を分類することを目的として設計されていないことである。
translation: レビュー過程において、ONHおよびMNHの両方を、EyeLink Parser（SR Research Ltd, オタワ, オンタリオ州, カナダ）および現代的な機械学習ベースの眼球運動分類アルゴリズム（Zemblys, Niehorster, Komogortsev, & Holmqvist, 2018）という2つの追加アルゴリズムと比較することに合意した。EyeLink Parserは、本稿で使用されているEyeLink 1000と同様のEyeLink眼球運動装置とともに提供される。この比較により、MNHの性能を非常に一般的に用いられる代替アルゴリズムと比較して記録することができた。重要な点として、EyeLink Parserはリアルタイム、オンラインアルゴリズムであり、PSO（サッケード後振動）を分類することを目的として設計されていないことである。

source: To illustrate the variability in these adaptive thresholds and the kurtosis from subject to subject, we present the adaptive saccade thresholds and kurtosis for the 20 subjects in the present study in Table 2. As a general matter, the saccade peak velocity thresholds computed for our data are in the range of 10°–20°/s, which is substantially lower than the 33°/s reported by Nystrӧm and Holmqvist (2010). Our data are substantially less noisy than the data they report on. Note that this is true even though we employed a muchshorter, and thus potentially noisier, smoothing window for the calculation of velocity. Note the high intersubject variability in these thresholds, as well as the extremely high thresholds and the extremely high measure of kurtosis for one subject.
draft: これらの適応的閾値および被験者間の尖度の変動を示すために、本研究における20名の被験者の適応的サッケード閾値および尖度を表2に示す。一般的に、本研究データで計算されたサッケードピーク速度閾値は10°–20°/sの範囲にあるが、これはNystrӧmとHolmqvist（2010）が報告した33°/sよりも著しく低い。本研究のデータは、彼らが報告しているデータよりも著しくノイズが少ない。なお、速度の計算に非常に短い、したがって潜在的にノイズが多い平滑化ウィンドウを使用したにもかかわらず、この事実は成り立つ。これらの閾値における高い被験者間変動、および1名の被験者の極めて高い閾値および極めて高い尖度の測定値に注目されたい。
translation: これらの適応的閾値および被験者間の尖度の変動を示すために、本研究における20名の被験者の適応的サッケード閾値および尖度を表2に示す。一般的に、本研究データで計算されたサッケードピーク速度閾値は10°–20°/sの範囲にあるが、これはNystrӧmとHolmqvist（2010）が報告した33°/sよりも著しく低い。本研究のデータは、彼らが報告しているデータよりも著しくノイズが少ない。なお、速度の計算に非常に短い、したがって潜在的にノイズが多い平滑化ウィンドウを使用したにもかかわらず、この事実は成り立つ。これらの閾値における高い被験者間変動、および1名の被験者の極めて高い閾値および極めて高い尖度の測定値に注目されたい。

source: There were three human raters, all of whom are authors on this report. Rater BL{v1}has been studying eye movements, on and off, for more than 25 years. He has 12 peer-reviewed publications that report on eye movement results. He is also the programmer who created the MNH. source: Although generally the MNH far outperformed the ONH, the MNH is clearly not perfect, and certain aspects of it could be improved. For example, although there were fewer saccade timing errors with this method, there werestill a substantial num- ber of such errors. In our view, to further improve the perfor- mance of the MNH for saccade timing, the position trace signals need to be taken into consideration as well as the velocity trace. The performance of the MNH in detecting very small saccades could be improved by the development of a special subroutine devoted to this task. A simple solution of lowering the fixed saccade velocity detection thresholds might work, or it might create unforeseen issues with the scoring of other events. In the future, we plan to try several approaches to deal with this issue.

source: With respect to the machine-learning-based algorithm, the concern was that the ONH was not considered to be a state-of- the-art algorithm at this time, and that an improvement on it would possibly also not be competitive with state-of-the-art algorithms. The algorithm of Zemblys et al. (2018) was cho- sen because it is considered a modern, state-of-the-art algo- rithm, because it classifies PSOs in addition to fixations and saccades, and because it was simple for us to have our data scoredwith this method. The Zemblys et al. algorithm is based on a machine-learning approach termed BRandom Forest,{v1}and thus Zemblys et al. refer to the algorithm as the IRF. At the time that the decision to also evaluate these two compar- isons was made, two members of the algorithm evaluation panel (authors E.A. and I.R.) were no longer involved, so these two additionial comparisons were based on a single evaluator (author L.F.). For comprehensive reviews of eye movement methods, see Andersson et al. (2017), Hein and Zangemeister (2017), and Salvucci and Goldberg (2000).

source: There are several general impressions that one has after reviewing the classification results from the IRF. draft: IRFからの分類結果を検討した後、いくつかの一般的な印象が得られる。まず、肯定的な側面として、このアルゴリズムはサッケードのタイミングに関して驚くほど正確である。サッケードの開始タイミングが早すぎたり遅すぎたりするものを見つけることはできなかったという事実は、非常に顕著である。また、サッケードの終了タイミングについては、開始タイミングほど完璧ではないものの、極めて良好であった。サッケードのタイミングに関しては、IRFが断然優れている。これは評価結果を検討した際に明らかになるだろう。

source: Filter the data Smooth the data and compute the smoothed position trace, smoothed velocity trace, and smoothed accel- eration trace. Both the ONH and the MNH use the Savitzky– Golay filter function sgolay to compute filter coefficients (Both algorithms were written in Matlab code and run in Matlab {v1}Version R2015b; The MathWorks, Natick, MA{v2}.) Both algorithms employ the filter routine to apply the filter coefficients, to compute the smoothed position signal, the ve- locity signal and the acceleration signal. Note that despite the claims by Nystrӧm and Holmqvist (2010, p. 192), the filter delay is not removed. Use of the convfunction (convolution), as in conv(X,g(:,1),’same’), where X is the signal and g are the filter coefficients, would have removed the delay. Use of the sgolayfilt function would also have removed the delay. Note that, for 1000 Hz, the ONH filter width was 19 samples (i.e., 19 ms), but MNH changes this to 7 ms. Both algorithms used the same filter order—that is, 2.

source: Recent findings have called into question the usefulness and accuracy of video-based eyetrackers, which rely on esti- mates of the pupil position and the corneal reflection position (Hooge et al., 2016; Nystrom et al., 2013). PSOs in particular are seen, at least partially, to be an artifact of the differing temporal dynamics of the pupil and the corneal reflection. The claim is also made that these devices are not suitable for studying the detailed dynamics of eye movements. We have nothing to contribute to this discussion, and we leave it to the user to decide whether or not to treat the PSOs detectedby the MNH as eye movements. Perhaps some may choose to in- clude PSO time in the postsaccadic fixation period. We want to simply state that, to define PSO events, we relied on the definitions provided in Nyström and Holmqvist (2010), par- ticularly as displayed in their Figs. 1 and 9. We are not aware of any retraction on the part of these authors as to this defini- tion of the appearance of PSOs in recordings from video- oculographic eye movement recording systems.
draft: 最近の知見は、瞳孔位置および角膜反射位置の推定に依存する動画ベースのアイトラッキング装置の有用性と正確性を疑問視している（Hooge et al., 2016; Nystrom et al., 2013）。特にPSO（サッケード後振動）は、瞳孔と角膜反射の時間的ダイナミクスの相違に起因するアーティファクトであると考えられている。また、これらの装置が眼球運動の詳細なダイナミクスを研究するのに適していないという主張もある。我々はこの議論に対して何ら貢献するものがないため、ユーザーにPSO（サッケード後振動）がMNHによって検出された場合、それを眼球運動として扱うかどうかを判断してもらう。一部の研究者が、サッケード後の固視期間にPSO（サッケード後振動）の時間を含める選択をするかもしれない。我々は単に、PSO（サッケード後振動）イベントを定義する際、NyströmとHolmqvist（2010）が提示した定義に依拠したことを述べたい。この動画眼運動記録システムにおけるPSO（サッケード後振動）の出現の定義に関して、これらの著者から撤回があることを我々は認識していない。

Although the evaluation approach described by Andersson et al. was not used to detect the kinds of classification errors we will emphasize in this report, it seems likely that their approach could be modified to provide such data. However, since this evaluation method requires human experts to clas- sify, in many recordings, every sample as belonging to one event type or another, this is a very cumbersome and ineffi- cient method to get the kind of classification error counts that we seek, especially when comparing only two or three algo- rithms. However, we concede that the approach of Andersson et al. would probably be faster when comparing more than three algorithms.

source: To compare the error rates between methods, we employed the sign test (Siegel & Castellan, 1988). This is a paired test that converts each comparison between an ONH scoring and an MNH scoring for the same subject (a set) as a series of ones and zeros. If the ONH is greater than the MNH, this is represent- ed as a 1. If the MNH is greater than the ONH, this is represented as a 0. The sign testevaluates the probability of getting X number of ones for Y trials (in this case, Y {v1}trials). Effect sizes (Cohen’s d; Cohen, 1988) were calculated for these tests by converting from an exact p value (15 digits) to a Z score. The Z score was converted to an equivalent Pearson r correlation coefficient, which was then converted to Cohen’s d (Cooper & Hedges, 1994). Given the precision of the computer system, the maximum d that could be estimated was 17.1, a truly giant effect size.
draft: 各手法間の誤差率を比較するため、符号検定（Siegel & Castellan, 1988）を用いた。これは対応のある検定であり、同一被験者（セット）に対するONHスコアとMNHスコアの各比較を1と0の系列に変換する。ONHがMNHより大きい場合、これを1として表す。MNHがONHより大きい場合、これを0として表す。符号検定は、Y回の試行（この場合、Y {v1}回の試行）においてX個の1を得る確率を評価する。これらの検定について効果量（Cohenのd；Cohen, 1988）は、正確なp値（15桁）からZスコアに変換することにより算出された。Zスコアは等価なピアソンr相関係数に変換され、その後Cohenのdに変換された（Cooper & Hedges, 1994）。コンピュータシステムの精度を考慮すると、推定可能な最大のdは17.1であり、これは本当に巨大な効果量である。

source: The main findings of this part of the study are that our modified version of the Nystrӧm and Holmqvist (2010) algorithm (MNH) has markedly fewer errors in the timing of the onset and offset of saccades and the number of undetected fixations and saccades thantheoriginal algorithm (ONH; Nyström & Holmqvist, 2010). In a small, but not insignificant, number of subjects, the ONH completely fails (our best estimate is in 8.3% of subjects). The MNH does underperform with respect to the ONH, however, in the detection of very small saccades. As a result, the MNH scores significantly more fixations, fewer saccades, more PSOs, and leaves fewer periods unclassified than does the ONH. Also, data scored by the MNH result in significantly more time in fixation, significantly less time in saccades, and much less time in unclas- sified periods than does the ONH.
draft: 本研究のこの部分における主な findings は、Nystrӧm および Holmqvist (2010) のアルゴリズムの修正版（MNH）が、オリジナル版アルゴリズム（ONH；Nyström & Holmqvist, 2010）と比較して、サッケードの開始および終了のタイミングにおける誤差、検出されなかった固視およびサッケードの数が著しく少ないことである。少数の被験者においては、ONH は完全に失敗する（我々の最良の推定では被験者の8.3％で発生する）。しかし、非常に小さなサッケードの検出に関しては、MNH は ONH よりも性能が劣る。その結果、MNH は ONH と比較して有意に多くの固視、少ないサッケード、より多くのPSO（サッケード後振動）、そして未分類の期間が少なくなる。また、MNH によってスコア付けされたデータは、ONH と比較して有意に長い固視時間、有意に短いサッケード時間、および著しく短い未分類期間を示す。

source: Priorto classifying the main set of 20 subjects, all raters practiced on four Btraining subjects,{v1}each scored by both algorithms (eight studies). During this period, open discussion between the raters was encouraged. source: We found the following issues with the ONH as applied to our data: (1) In our view, it uses too much smoothing of the position and velocity signals; (2) it uses a threshold for ex- tending an artifact forward and backward in time that is much too small for our data; (3) it uses nonoptimal metrics to define the central tendency and spread of the highly skewed fixation velocity noise distribution; (4) the adaptive thresholds it com- putes for our data are unreasonably small, (5) by not consid- ering the position trace, it consistently marks the start of sac- cades too early and the end of saccades too late; and (6) bynot allowing fixation periods to start or end with artifact, it dra- matically underscores fixation. Because of these issues with the ONH, as applied to our data, the ONH scores many more saccades as starting too early, or ending too late, and it fails to detect many fixations.
draft: 我々は、ONHを自らのデータに適用した場合に以下の問題を発見した：（1）我々の見解では、位置信号および速度信号の平滑化がやりすぎである；（2）時間的に前後へとアーティファクトを延長するための閾値が、自らのデータに対してはあまりにも小さすぎる；（3）極めて歪んだ固視速度雑音分布の中心傾向および散らばりを定義するための最適でない指標を使用している；（4）自らのデータに対して計算される適応的閾値が、妥当性に欠けるほど小さすぎる；（5）位置トレースを考慮しないことにより、サッケードの開始を常に早めにマークし、サッケードの終了を常に遅くマークしてしまう；および（6）固視期間がアーティファクトで始まることや終わることを許容しないため、固視を著しく強調してしまう。これらのONHの問題点により、自らのデータに適用した場合、ONHは多くのサッケードを開始が早すぎる、または終了が遅すぎるものとしてマークし、多くの固視を検出できなくなってしまう。

source: In general, the EyeLink Parser performs very well when de- termining saccade onset. However, a large number of saccades ended too early. The EyeLink Parserdoes a reasonably good job determining the end of saccades in the absence of PSOs. But in the presence of PSOs, we find many saccades that end too late and include a portion of the following PSO.

source: assumption was completely unsupported. These distributions were highly skewed. We hypothesize that any such distribu- tion, from any similar dataset, would be similarly skewed. A measure of skewness is kurtosis. For a normal distribution, the kurtosis should be near 3.0. Below we present the kurtosis for each of the 20 datasets employed in this study. The median kurtosis was 7.56. Also, tests of normality (Pearson chi-square goodness-of-fit tests) indicated that these distributions were not normal (all p values were essentially 0.0, meaning that we can reject the null hypothesis that the distribution was drawn from a normal population). source: We think that the present method used to evaluate error types provides an unusually rich source of information for an algorithm developer. source: Our analysis of the IRF machine-learning algorithm of Zemblys et al. (2018) revealed several serious flaws in the output of this method. Although the IRF is amazingly accurate for saccade timing, there were a number of serious problems with the output of this method. Although the IRF algorithm states that it includes a number of postprocessing steps de- signed to remove unusual events, the evidence suggests that many postprocessing steps wereeither inadequately applied or not applied at all. Without these postprocessing steps, the out- put of the IRF is so replete with errors that we cannot recom- mend its use at this time.

These pre-processing steps followed the method used previously in our laboratory to remove noise for saccade detec- tion with a velocity threshold. However, these pre-processing steps could be replaced by any pre-processing steps that sufficiently increase the signal-to-noise ratio.

source: Despite a significant increase in the use of eye movements in neuroscience, there have been very few advances in the algorithms used to detect fixations and saccades (Salvucci and Goldberg, 2000). We could only find a few instances of algorithms that deviated sig- nificantly from the most widely used algorithms. Unfortunately, many of these alternative algorithms still employ a velocity thresh- old to detect potential saccades, followed by additional techniques including principal component analysis to distinguish between smooth pursuit, saccades, and noise (Berg et al., 2009; Liston et al., 2012). One exception is (Urruty et al., 2007) which used dispersion and projection clustering into arbitrary subspace to detect fixa- tions. To the best of our knowledge, these algorithms have not been adopted in subsequent studies.
draft: 神経科学における眼球運動の使用が著しく増加したにもかかわらず、固視およびサッケードを検出するためのアルゴリズムにはほとんど進展が見られない（Salvucci and Goldberg, 2000）。最も広く使われているアルゴリズムから著しく逸脱したアルゴリズムの例はわずかしか見つけることができなかった。残念なことに、これらの代替アルゴリズムの多くは、潜在的なサッケードを検出するために速度閾値を用いるものであり、その後、主成分分析などの追加的手法を用いて滑動性追従眼球運動、サッケード、雑音を区別している（Berg et al., 2009; Liston et al., 2012）。唯一の例外は（Urruty et al., 2007）であり、分散度および任意の部分空間への投影クラスタリングを用いて固視を検出していた。我々が知る限り、これらのアルゴリズムはその後の研究で採用されていない。
translation: 神経科学における眼球運動の使用が著しく増加したにもかかわらず、固視およびサッケードを検出するためのアルゴリズムにはほとんど進展が見られない（Salvucci and Goldberg, 2000）。最も広く使われているアルゴリズムから著しく逸脱したアルゴリズムの例はわずかしか見つけることができなかった。残念なことに、これらの代替アルゴリズムの多くは、潜在的なサッケードを検出するために速度閾値を用いるものであり、その後、主成分分析などの追加的手法を用いて滑動性追従眼球運動、サッケード、雑音を区別している（Berg et al., 2009; Liston et al., 2012）。唯一の例外は（Urruty et al., 2007）であり、分散および任意の部分空間への投影クラスタリングを用いて固視を検出していた。我々が知る限り、これらのアルゴリズムはその後の研究で採用されていない。

source: Here we present a novel algorithm, called Cluster Fix, which applies k-means cluster analysis to parse scan paths into fixa- tions and saccades. There are several clear qualitative differences between fixations and saccades—saccades are temporally short with a high velocity whereas fixations are longer in duration with a slower velocity. These qualitative differences translate into quan- titative differences and the occupation of different regions in state space. Cluster Fix makes no assumptions about the arrangement of scan paths in state space, requires no human inputs, and includes only duration thresholds as free parameters.
draft: ここでは、k-meansクラスタ分析を用いてスキャンパスを固視とサッケードに分解する新しいアルゴリズム、Cluster Fix を提示する。固視とサッケードの間にはいくつか明確な定性的な違いがある—サッケードは時間的に短く、速度が高いため、一方固視は持続時間が長く、速度が遅い。これらの定性的な違いは定量的な違いに翻訳され、状態空間内の異なる領域を占める。Cluster Fix はスキャンパスの状態空間における配置についていかなる仮定も行わず、人間の入力を必要とせず、自由パラメータとして持つのは時間的閾値のみである。
translation: ここでは、k-meansクラスタ分析を用いてスキャンパスを固視とサッケードに分解する新しいアルゴリズム、Cluster Fix を提示する。固視とサッケードの間にはいくつか明確な定性的な違いがある—サッケードは時間的に短く、速度が高いため、一方固視は持続時間が長く、速度が遅い。これらの定性的な違いは定量的な違いに翻訳され、状態空間内の異なる領域を占める。Cluster Fix はスキャンパスの状態空間における配置についていかなる仮定も行わず、人間の入力を必要とせず、自由パラメータとして持つのは時間的閾値のみである。

source: Next, the absolute value of 4 state space parameters—distance, velocity, acceleration, and angular velocity—were calculated for every time point. Velocity and acceleration were computed as the first and second derivative of position, respectively. Distance was measured as the Euclidian distance between the position of the scan path at a time point to the position of the scan path two time points later. Angular velocity was calculated as the difference in the angle of the scan path from one time point to the next. Angular veloc- ity was subtracted from {v1}so that lower values were associated with fixations. For each state space parameter, any values greater than 3 standard deviations above the mean were set to 3 standard deviations above the mean, and all values were then normalized from 0 to 1.
draft: 次に、4つの状態空間パラメータ—距離、速度、加速度、および角速度—の絶対値を、すべての時刻点について計算した。速度と加速度は、それぞれ位置の1次および2次の微分として計算された。距離は、時刻点におけるスキャンパスの位置から2つの時刻点後のスキャンパスの位置までのユークリッド距離として測定された。角速度は、1つの時刻点から次の時刻点へのスキャンパスの角度の差として計算された。角速度は{v1}から差し引かれたため、低い値が固視に関連付けられた。各状態空間パラメータについて、平均値より3標準偏差以上大きいすべての値は、平均値より3標準偏差の値に設定され、その後すべての値は0から1の範囲に正規化された。

source: Algorithms employing velocity and acceleration thresholds for saccade detection may be sufficient for simple tasks in which subjects make predictable saccades toward a stationary target; however, more complex oculomotor tasks such as unconstrained viewing of natural scenes or dynamic stimuli may produce more variable eye movements (Andrews and Coppola, 1999; Hayhoe and Ballard, 2005; Berg et al., 2009; Rayner, 2009). A major source of this variability arises from the variability in saccade amplitude which is strongly correlated with the peak velocity of the saccade (Otero- Millan et al., 2008; Martinez-Conde et al., 2009, 2013). Velocity thresholds may not accurately parse highly variable scan paths into periods of fixations and saccades since saccade amplitudes and thus their peak velocity are not constrained in free viewing. Further, many algorithms employ arbitrary thresholds based on qualitative human observations which can vary across research laboratories and even from one experiment to the next within a laboratory. Finally, computed viewing behavior statistics includ- ing saccade rate, fixation duration, saccade duration, and saccade amplitude vary not only according to experimental variables but also by the method used to calculate them (Duchowski, 2007; Shic et al., 2008; Nystrom and Holmqvist, 2010). Therefore, there exists a need for a more accurate, sensitive, non-arbitrary, and completely automated saccade detection algorithm. Such an algo- rithm could constitute a “gold standard” for detecting fixations and saccades from scan paths so that viewing behavior could be accurately compared across experiments, laboratories, and algo- rithms.
draft: 速度および加速度閾値を用いるアルゴリズムは、被験者が静止したターゲットに向けて予測可能なサッケードを行うような単純なタスクには十分である場合があるが、自然なシーンや動的刺激の自由視認のようなより複雑な眼球運動タスクでは、より変動性の高い眼球運動が生じる可能性がある（Andrews and Coppola, 1999; Hayhoe and Ballard, 2005; Berg et al., 2009; Rayner, 2009）。この変動性の主要な原因は、サッケード振幅の変動であり、これはサッケードのピーク速度と強く相関している（Otero-Millan et al., 2008; Martinez-Conde et al., 2009, 2013）。自由視認ではサッケード振幅およびそのピーク速度が制約されないため、速度閾値は変動性の高いスキャンパスを固視とサッケードの期間に正確に分割できない可能性がある。さらに、多くのアルゴリズムは定性的な人間観察に基づく任意の閾値を使用しており、これは研究室間で異なり、また同一研究室内の異なる実験間でも変動する可能性がある。最後に、計算された視認行動統計量であるサッケード頻度、固視持続時間、サッケード持続時間およびサッケード振幅は、実験変数だけでなく、それらを計算する手法にも依存して変化する（Duchowski, 2007; Shic et al., 2008; Nystrom and Holmqvist, 2010）。したがって、より正確で感度が高く、任意性がなく、完全に自動化されたサッケード検出アルゴリズムの必要性が存在する。このようなアルゴリズムは、スキャンパスからの固視およびサッケードの検出における「ゴールドスタンダード」となる可能性があり、視認行動を実験間、研究室間、アルゴリズム間で正確に比較できるようになる。

source: Scan paths were obtained at 200 Hz using an infrared eye tracker (ISCAN) from rhesus macaques freely viewing 288 images of natural scenes. Eye tacking data were collected from 4 adult male macaques seated head-fixed in a dimly illuminated room 60 cm away from a 19 in. CRT monitor with a refresh rate of 120 Hz. Images of nat- ural scenes were {v1}pixels large and subtended {v2}of visual angle (dva). Experimental control software (CORTEX http://dally.nimh.nih.gov/) displayed images for 10 s each. Initial calibration of the infrared eye tracking system consisted of a 9- point calibration task. Drift was tracked throughout the experiment by presenting additional calibration trials between image view- ing trials. We excluded from further analysis any eye tracking data more than 50 pixels (2 dva) outside of the image. Blinks were rarely observed in our data so we did not make any corrections other than the exclusion of data outside of the image. Standard blink cor- rection techniques should work with Cluster Fix if scan paths are evaluated in a piece-wise manner ignoring blinks and as long as at least one fixation is present in each evaluated portion of the scan path (Supplementary Fig. 1). All experiments were carried out in accordance with the National Institutes of Health guidelines and were approved by the Emory University Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee and Emory Institutional Review Board.

source: Cluster Fix globally clustered every time point in state space into k number of clusters. We determined the appropriate number of clusters using the average silhouette width (MATLAB function SILHOUETTE). The silhouette width measures the average ratio of inter- and intra-cluster distances to determine the appropri- ate number of clusters. Higher ratio values indicate that points within clusters were closer to each other than points outside of their respective clusters. We chose the number of possible clus- ters to be from 2 to 5 clusters because in a typical scan path there is at least 1 fixation and 1 saccade, and in the most complex scan path we can divide fixations into 2 separate clusters and saccades into 3 separate clusters. Fixations can be subdivided into 2 clusters: one with low angular velocity and one with high angular velocity. Saccades can be subdivided into 3 clusters: low velocity but high acceleration, low acceleration but high velocity, and high velocity and high acceleration.
draft: Cluster Fixは、状態空間内のすべての時系列点をk個のクラスタにグローバルにクラスタリングした。適切なクラスタ数は平均シルエット幅（MATLAB関数SILHOUETTE）を用いて決定した。シルエット幅は、クラスタ間距離とクラスタ内距離の平均比を測定し、適切なクラスタ数を判断する。高い比値は、クラスタ内の点がそれぞれのクラスタ外の点よりも近いことを示している。典型的なスキャンパスには少なくとも1つの固視と1つのサッケードが存在するため、可能なクラスタ数を2から5までとした。最も複雑なスキャンパスにおいては、固視を2つの別個のクラスタに分割し、サッケードを3つの別個のクラスタに分割できる。固視は2つのクラスタに細分化できる：低角速度のクラスタと高角速度のクラスタである。サッケードは3つのクラスタに細分化できる：低速度だが高加速度、低加速度だが高速度、および高速度かつ高加速度のクラスタである。

source: Fig. 4. Thresholds vs. Cluster Fix. Fixations (red) and saccades (green) determined through Cluster Fix for an example segment of a scan path. Velocity (A) and acceleration (B) thresholds (black lines, mean {v1}std) appear to miss smaller amplitude saccades either due to velocity or acceleration values not exceeding the threshold (purple {v2}#1) or values did not exceeded the threshold for a sufficient duration (purple {v3}#2). (C) A 2D state space plot indicates that single-value thresholds may misclassify fixation and saccade time points which may be critical to properly identify the onset and offset of saccades. Note that because velocity and accelerations values were normalized to the mean plus 3 times the standard deviation many saccade time points are located on the edge of the plot. Also, note that up-sampling and low pass filtering creates an appearance of arc-like patterns in state space.

source: We are confident that Cluster Fix can correctly identify smaller saccades because these smaller saccades were identified by finding natural divisions in scan paths, and these smaller saccades occupied different regions of state space than fixations. Visual inspection of the scan paths supports this conclusion as well. Identification of smaller saccades was more difficult when the smaller saccades were surrounded by highly variable fixations in comparison to smaller saccades surrounded by less noisy fixations. Further, iden- tification of these smaller saccades often served to break up longer “fixations,” detected by global clustering, into more appropriate length fixations.
draft: クラスターフィクスは、より小さなサッケードを正しく識別できることに確信している。なぜなら、これらのより小さなサッケードはスキャンパス内の自然な分割を見つけることで同定されたからであり、それらのより小さなサッケードは固視とは異なる状態空間の領域を占めていたからである。スキャンパスの視覚的検査もこの結論を支持している。より小さなサッケードが非常に変動の大きい固視に囲まれている場合、それらのより小さなサッケードの同定は、より小さなサッケードがノイズの少ない固視に囲まれている場合よりも困難であった。さらに、これらのより小さなサッケードの同定は、しばしばグローバルクラスタリングによって検出された長い「固視」を、より適切な長さの固視に分割する役割を果たした。

source: Fig. 1. Global clustering in scan path state space. (A) Global clustering identified the appropriate number of clusters in 4 state space parameters—distance (not shown), velocity, acceleration, and angular velocity—normalized from 0 to 1. Each dot represents a single time point (1 ms) from a representative scan path (yellow lines overlaying image in inset) with each color representing a different cluster. Blue and brown clusters represent time points with low acceleration and velocity. These two clusters represent the two states of fixation (high and low angular velocity). Pink, gold, and turquoise clusters represent clusters with higher velocity and acceleration. These three clusters represent the three states of saccades. (B) Representative section of the up-sampled scan path globally clustered in A (indicated by purple circle in inset image). Each cluster represents a different portion of the scan path across multiple fixations or saccades. (C) Fixation clusters (red) were determined as the clusters with the lowest velocity and acceleration. All other clusters were classified as saccades (green). (D) The same portion of the scan path now parsed into fixations and saccades. (E) Following local re-clustering many of the fixation time points were reclassified as the beginning and end of saccades. Additionally, re-classification reduced the size of the fixation cluster and resulted in some fixation and saccade time points overlapping in state space. (F) Representative section of the final raw scan path parsed into fixations and saccades.

source: Future work could improve Cluster Fix by adding parameters or adaptations to detect eye movements that are neither fixations nor saccades such as smooth pursuit. The largest challenge in detecting smooth pursuit would be determining the best way to consolidate clusters. With Cluster Fix each cluster represents tangible aspects of the scan path. Typically, in our binary classification, we find a saccade cluster with high velocity and low acceleration, and this cluster often represents periods of consecutive time points in the scan path. With the right selection of clusters and duration thresh- olds we see no reason why one could not identify periods of smooth pursuit with Cluster Fix.
draft: 今後の研究では、滑動性追従眼球運動など、固視でもサッケードでもない眼球運動を検出できるように、Cluster Fixにパラメータや適応を追加することで改善が可能である。滑動性追従眼球運動を検出する上で最大の課題は、クラスタを統合する最良の方法を決定することである。Cluster Fixでは各クラスタがスキャンパスの実体的な側面を表す。通常、我々の二値分類においては、高速度かつ低加速度のサッケードクラスタを見つけることができ、このクラスタはしばしばスキャンパスにおける連続する時系列ポイントの期間を表す。適切なクラスタおよび持続時間閾値の選択により、Cluster Fixで滑動性追従眼球運動の期間を同定することは全く問題ないと考えられる。

source: A common practice in the analysis of human eye movement data is to operationally define saccades that are smaller than 1 dva in amplitude as microsaccades (Engbert and Kliegl, 2003; Otero- Millan et al., 2008; Martinez-Conde et al., 2013). Here we did not distinguish between microsaccades and saccades albeit approxi- mately 4% of the observed saccades had amplitudes of less than 1 dva (not equivalent to saccade arc length in Table 2). We observed that a large portion of these saccades were detected during “com- plex fixations” in which the eye covered a substantially larger area of the image for longer durations than most fixations. Often these “complex fixations” were observed when monkeys looked at complex objects such as faces and may have included rapid eye movements not clearly distinguishable at a sampling rate of 200 Hz. Therefore, we do not know if Cluster Fix is sufficient for detecting microsaccades or other fixational eye movements often observed at higher sampling frequencies (Martinez-Conde et al., 2009).
draft: 人間の眼球運動データ解析における一般的な手法は、振幅が1 dva未満のサッケードをマイクロサッケードとして操作的に定義することである（EngbertとKliegl, 2003；Otero-Millanら, 2008；Martinez-Condeら, 2013）。本研究では、マイクロサッケードとサッケードの区別を行わなかったが、観測されたサッケードの約4%は振幅が1 dva未満であった（表2におけるサッケード弧長とは等価ではない）。これらのサッケードの大部分が、「複雑な固視」中に検出されたことを見出した。この「複雑な固視」では、眼が画像の著しく広い領域を、大多数の固視よりも長時間にわたりカバーしていた。しばしば、サッケードは顔などの複雑な物体を観察している際、観察された。これらの「複雑な固視」には、200 Hzのサンプリング周波数では明確に区別できない速い眼運動が含まれていた可能性がある。したがって、サンプリング周波数が高い場合に頻繁に観察されるマイクロサッケードや他の固視微動を検出するのに、Cluster Fixが十分であるかどうかは不明である（Martinez-Condeら, 2009）。

source: A primary goal of this work was to create an algorithm that would be easy to implement across laboratories for a variety of behavioral tasks. For this reason, the algorithm was devised in MAT- LAB using commonly available functions. However, this algorithm may be enhanced through the use of better clustering algorithms as well as alternative ways for determining the appropriate number of clusters such as statistical measures (e.g. explanation of variance), visual inspection, the separation of clusters, and stability of clus- ters with resampling (Ben-Hur et al., 2002; Dudoit and Fridlyand, 2002; Pham et al., 2005). Cluster Fix requires approximately 240 s to analyze 720 s of eye data sampled at 200 Hz (MATLAB 2012b, Intel Core Xeon Processor 2.80 GHz with 16 GB RAM). This is sig- nificantly slower than an algorithm using velocity and acceleration thresholds which requires only a few seconds to analyze the same amount of data. The two dispersion-based algorithms analyzed scan paths substantially slower than Cluster Fix, but optimization of these algorithms could substantially increase the speed of analy- sis. In Cluster Fix nearly 80% of the computation time is devoted to determining the number of clusters of which nearly 90% is devoted to local re-clustering. Cluster Fix sacrifices time for a significant increase in sensitivity and specificity. Cluster Fix may run faster by parallelizing local re-clustering or compiling Cluster Fix in a different programming language optimized for cluster analysis.
draft: 本研究の主な目的の一つは、さまざまな行動タスクにおいて、複数の研究室で容易に実装可能なアルゴリズムを構築することであった。このため、アルゴリズムは一般的に利用可能な関数を用いてMATLABで設計された。しかし、より優れたクラスタリングアルゴリズムの使用およびクラスタ数の適切な決定方法（例えば分散度の説明、視覚的検査、クラスタ間の分離、再標本化におけるクラスタの安定性など）を用いることで、このアルゴリズムはさらに向上させることができる（Ben-Hur et al., 2002; Dudoit and Fridlyand, 2002; Pham et al., 2005）。Cluster Fixは、200 Hzでサンプリングされた720秒の眼動データを解析するのに約240秒を要する（MATLAB 2012b、Intel Core Xeonプロセッサ 2.80 GHz、16 GB RAM）。これは、速度および加速度のしきい値を使用するアルゴリズムと比較して著しく遅く、同じ量のデータを解析するには数秒しか要しない。分散度に基づく二つのアルゴリズムは、Cluster Fixよりも顕著に遅くスキャンパスを解析したが、これらのアルゴリズムの最適化により、解析速度は大幅に向上させることができる。Cluster Fixでは計算時間の約80％がクラスタ数の決定に費やされており、そのうち約90％が局所的な再クラスタリングに割り当てられている。Cluster Fixは、感度および特異度の著しい向上を実現するために、処理時間を犠牲にしている。局所的な再クラスタリングを並列化するか、クラスタ分析に最適化された別のプログラミング言語でCluster Fixをコンパイルすることで、Cluster Fixはより高速に実行可能である。

source: For a given subject, parameter values across multiple images were consistent for fixations, and fixation clusters did not overlap in state space with saccade clusters. This consistency demonstrates the plausibility of analyzing viewing behavior across multiple images using a single scan path as a template. During a practice trial, fixation and saccade clusters could quickly be determined as well as which areas of state space belong to each cluster using a classifi- cation algorithm such as a support vector machine. For subsequent experimental trials, for each time point, the position in state space could be classified as a fixation or saccade. With the addition of a duration threshold, these classifications could be used to determine when fixations and saccades occur in near real-time. Real-time detection of eye movements is essential for gaze-contingent exper- iments in which trial parameters depend on the subject’s viewing behavior. Other applications of Cluster Fix could include using the algorithm to determine proper velocity and acceleration thresh- olds for novel or complex tasks instead of trying to determine these thresholds empirically.
draft: 特定の被験者について、複数の画像におけるパラメータ値は固視において一貫しており、固視クラスタとサッケードクラスタは状態空間内で重複しなかった。この一貫性は、単一のスキャンパスをテンプレートとして用いて複数の画像における視認行動を分析する可能性を示している。練習試行において、サポートベクターマシンなどの分類アルゴリズムを用いることで、固視およびサッケードクラスタを迅速に決定し、状態空間内のどの領域がそれぞれのクラスタに属するかを特定することができた。その後の実験試行では、各時刻における状態空間内の位置を固視またはサッケードとして分類することができた。持続時間の閾値を追加することで、固視およびサッケードが近似的にリアルタイムで発生するタイミングを特定することができる。眼球運動のリアルタイム検出は、試行パラメータが被験者の視認行動に依存する視線連動実験において不可欠である。クラスタ固視の他の応用として、新しいまたは複雑なタスクにおける適切な速度および加速度閾値を、経験的に決定しようとする代わりに、このアルゴリズムを用いて決定することができる。

source: When choosing state space parameters, we took what we quali- tatively observed as differences between fixations and saccades and turned these into quantifiable parameters. Distance was selected because, during a fixation, data points are compact and close to each other while data points are more dispersed during a sac- cade. Density-dispersion algorithms explicitly take advantage of this parameter. Velocity and acceleration parameters were cho- sen because the eye moves faster during a saccade than during a fixation. The angular velocity parameter accounts for the smooth linear-like movements of saccades while fixations appear irregular (at 200 Hz) with position fluctuating around an attended location.

source: To increase the sensitivity of the algorithm to smaller amplitude saccades, the algorithm reevaluated each fixation locally using the same method applied in global clustering (Fig. 2). The concept of local re-clustering is to analyze data at the appropriate scale (i.e. in between 2 “large” saccades detected by global clustering) to remove the over shadowing effects of the larger variability in the whole or global data. In local re-clustering, time points 50 ms (approximately the average saccade duration) prior to and following a detected fixation were re-clustered with the detected fixation. SILHOUETTE

source: A great deal of effort has been expended on determining or developing methods for determining the proper thresholds for threshold-based algorithms. Even if one threshold is found to be optimal for a scan path for one subject in one experiment, that threshold is not guaranteed to be appropriate for another sub- ject, experiment, or even the same subject on another trial. Our data support the idea that thresholds are suboptimal for detec- ting fixations and saccades. Velocity and acceleration thresholds are relatively fast and easy to implement but suffer from detection errors. Dispersion-based algorithms can be implemented relatively quickly in real-time and appear to detect the presence of fixations with relatively high accuracy. However, dispersion-based algo- rithms fail to accurately measure the transition times between fixations and saccades which are extremely important in under- standing potential neural correlates of eye movements.
draft: 閾値ベースのアルゴリズムにおける適切な閾値を決定するか、またはその決定方法を開発するための多大な努力が払われてきた。ある被験者においてある実験のスキャンパスに対して一つの閾値が最適であると判明したとしても、その閾値が他の被験者、他の実験、あるいは同じ被験者の別の試行においても適切であるとは保証されない。われわれのデータは、閾値が固視およびサッケードを検出する上で非最適であるという考えを支持している。速度および加速度の閾値は比較的高速かつ容易に実装可能であるが、検出誤差を引き起こす。分散度ベースのアルゴリズムはリアルタイムで比較的迅速に実装可能であり、固視の存在を相対的に高い精度で検出しているように見える。しかし、分散度ベースのアルゴリズムは、固視とサッケードとの間の遷移時間を正確に測定できず、これは眼球運動の潜在的な神経的相関を理解する上で極めて重要である。

source: was used iteratively on 20% of the time points to determine the k, between 1 and 5. The median of the best k was chosen for the final number of clusters. The additional possibly of only finding 1 optimal cluster was added in case the evaluated portion of the scan path only contained a single fixation and no saccades. For each clus- ter, the median velocity and median acceleration were identified. Then, the cluster with the lowest sum of these two values was con- sidered to consist of fixation time points. Because the number of time points in each cluster was relatively small, measures of the mean and standard deviation of each cluster were more sensitive to outliers. Therefore, additional fixation clusters were determined by finding clusters whose median velocity and acceleration over- lapped with the first fixation cluster in velocity and acceleration state space.
